Doom is great. I've got everything cranked to Ultra and it seems to work well with X-fire. I've got 2 7970s and I'm getting 60+fps even in hectic firefights.

It actually lives up to the hype believe it or not, at least the SP stuff. I've not messed with the MP at all and am still running around the campaign.

It's fast, there is no cover or regenerating health, and you'll actually get most of your health from melee kills. There are pickups if you want to ignore that, and you can turn the notification off if you want. Makes the game harder, which isn't necessarily a bad thing.

Plenty of health and ammo lying around on Hurt me Plenty difficulty. Enemies are fast, agile, and fairly smart for a shooter. Not going to pass a turing test or anything, but they climb, flank, and make pains of themselves as they should.

Looks amazing as well. Like I said, I have everything cranked to Ultra and it runs great on my system. i7 3770k, 7970 Ghz Ed. 6 Gb x2 in X-fire, 16 GB of Ram, and Windows 10. Smooth as silk and a consistently high framerate. Even with lowered settings it looks great.

Would not want to play this with a controller. That's just me because I'm spoiled by having a nice PC. It's the ugliest game I've ever played, in a good way, because it's hell and gore and stuff. This is the best looking game this year, possibly ever.

The animations are epic, the design of the monsters is pure horror, and it rewards exploration. You can bully your way through and head right for the goal, but you'll miss a lot doing that. It's best to take every path you can and explore, climb around, and at least attempt to make every jump that it looks like you might be able to make.

Highly recommend the new Doom. It's very much an updated version of the old school game, and nothing like Doom 3, which I also liked. The pacing here is very different, monsters swarm, stuff teleports in when you trigger a zone, and it's very much you against the horde. It seems to have taken some cues from the Brutal Doom mod, which is a good thing. It's actually a lot like Serious Sam 3, but better looking, and with smarter enemies.

The upgrade system is nice too. You don't ever have to mess with it as I understand it, but you're missing out if you don't. The only thing better than a shotgun is a shotgun with an alt fire mode that shoots explosive shells.

Doom lives up to the hype and is an improvement over Doom 3 in every way that matters. Just like Wolfenstein New Order, it's better than it has any right to be as a reboot.

EDIT: X-fire can be enabled, but does not work. The game only runs on one card even if it's on, the other card kicks on, but doesn't do anything and stays at 0% GPU load. So, I'm wrong about it working. Surprisingly, I'm getting legit performance with a single card. It drops to 30 when things get really hardcore in very busy areas with lots of particle effects, but mostly stays at 50+ during most fights, and 60 when I'm just wandering around. I do have V-sync enabled, because I was getting some tearing with it off. This is with all the settings maxed out BTW. My GPU is performing much better than I thought it would on one card, especially considering it's older and a lesser card than the recommended one. It's also worth noting that I'm playing at 1980, as that's my monitor's resolution.
